interrogate.verdict: The diagnosis is sound and the plan targets the owner's problem: a flat, capped scale with no tail, measured by bots. But the owner meets the fix only at step 6, after a six-tribe redesign and a bot rework. His own ask ("test it and see if it creates a good game ... does it feel like it has a nice flow") gets no play check before the redesign. Three bars are missing. Nothing passes or fails on how often snowballs happen (his main 9d worry). Nothing measures whether power jumps feel like progress. And S1's "board strength" has no unit that works across rounds. Two harness parts have no reader (hindsight search, the calibrated Health model). The step 5 bot rework is larger than the owner's "okay at best" calls for. Fix the bars, pull strong-field mode forward, and play a lever build on today's pool before step 4. Approve after that.
cut: DEFER Step 0 part 3, hindsight search (agent: critic 2 'missing'). Nothing in steps 2-4 reads it, and searching over buys through a seeded shop is the costliest part. Trigger: a redesigned tribe fails S1 low, or the scripted lines look weak, so it is checked before the tribe is redesigned again.

CUT Step 0 part 2, Health from 'a damage model calibrated on the lobby data' (orchestrator). Step 2's scripted-line lobbies already give real Health from real damage. A model calibrated on bot lobbies also goes against 9d and goes stale when L6 changes damage. Take S3's Health at round 8 from the line lobbies instead.

SHRINK Step 5 bots (rollouts, adaptive climbing, saving, answer buying; agent, Done means 4). The owner (9d): bots are 'okay at best', and making elite ones is 'harder than making the game'. Strong-field mode is already the playtest default. Keep answer buying on the scout and a climb-when-affordable fix. Defer rollouts until a playtest shows the bot seats matter.

SHRINK Step 2 full metric suite 'alone and in sensible combinations' (agent). Six levers times seven metric families exceeds two 3 GB Godot processes on 6 cores and 14 GB (LEARNINGS.md:66-68). Run S1 and upsets for each lever, and S2-S4, line lobbies and the screenshot only on the finalist set.
SHRINK readability check per lever. One phone screenshot at the finalist set's p99 numbers is enough.

SHRINK Step 1 reference-curves.md. Build it from the Firestone and replay data the audit already has (stat-scale-bg-galaxy.md, chart_stat_curve.json). Galaxy is optional and Battlegrounds is enough for target v1.

SHRINK Step 3 costing model (agent). If step 4 passes tribes on harness bars, the price table has no reader. v2 = target shape + harness bars + a too-small test. Re-set the gold table only if a named reader uses it (bot valuation, the costing reviewer).

SHRINK 'every path choice in steps 2-4 goes to adversarial critics' (orchestrator, widening the owner's 9c 'when you're unsure if a path is correct'). Send the adopted lever set, the scale spec, and the calls the orchestrator is unsure of.

ASK 'every tribe gets a route to a carry' (agent; fundamentals §3 itself leans toward non-carry routes for Bog and Oozes). Risks samey tribes against Done means 3. Make it: every tribe gets a compounding visible engine, and most get a carry route.
change: Define S1's unit. Field win rate is relative within a round (p50 is about 50% by construction), so it can't show growth by round, and the Battlegrounds reference is in stats. Use combat-start stats for the curve and the reference comparison, and field win rate for ranking and tribe bands, or add cross-round fights.

Step 0 Done: strong scripted lines should beat bots, so 'within the lobby data's band' may fail for the right reason. Check the shape instead (linear growth, no board at 2x the median), with the lines at or above the bot band.

Add a numeric snowball bar, the owner's main 9d concern, to step 2 Done and to each tribe's step 4 pass. For example: the round-8 leader wins at most 30% of line lobbies, the smaller board wins 14-26% of round 10-14 fights, and a set share of boards sit at 2x the median. Today these are reported but nothing fails on them.

Add a progression bar for the owner's 9c 'jumps in power level make the player actually feel stronger'. Measure a new-tier card's size against the board median, and climbing against staying and rolling at rounds 9, 12 and 14 (scored against the field 1-3 turns later). Today the only check is a critic's reading.

Step 2 says every lever is 'a data or config change', but L4 and L5 are engine work. The engine has no shield, cleave, damage reduction or venom, and target_select.gd only has highest_attack and highest_health. Build them once as reusable keywords that step 4's designers use.

Step 2 Done 'lands near target v1' may be unreachable on today's pool (one compounding card), and the fallback (grow variance before engines) is wrong if the cause is missing content. Make it a lever-response table plus one candidate set, with a time box.

Add an economy lever, or log why stats come first. The owner's 9d snowball runs economy to tempo to more economy. All six levers are stat levers, and everyone spends about 10 gold a round, so S3 would measure today's hollow economy.

Step 4: rewrite each tribe's scripted lines after its redesign, by an author other than its designers (or have a critic try to beat them). Otherwise a tribe's measured strength is its line author's skill. The step 0 lines are written for today's cards.

Step 4: say which field the pass bars fight while two tribes are new and four are old. Use step 2's adopted-lever lines as the reference field, refreshed as tribes land, or the old tribes skew S1 and S4.
Strong-field mode: say how the other seats lose Health and get eliminated, so placement and 'how far can I get' (Done means 4) still mean something.

Move to 'rules that hold throughout', from step 0: 'rare highrolls don't fail work' (9d), and Done means 2 rewritten so the lobby spread is only a sanity line. Otherwise the reviewers of steps 0-2 judge by the old bot-lobby bar.
Pull strong-field mode and field ghosts forward to right after step 2 (they reuse step 0's field). Ship a lever build on today's pool, and have reward-lens reviewers play it before step 4.
risks: The harness measures agent-written lines, so the curve and the tribe bands reflect line quality. A human with no timer may run many-action lines that are stronger than any script (fundamentals finding 13), so the sim tail may understate the real one.

No playable check before the six-tribe redesign. If compounding feels bad in play, it is found after all six tribes are rebuilt. This also breaks the 6 Nov plan-review rule: 'play a small slice first'.
Compute: two capped Godot processes on 6 cores and 14 GB. The step 2 matrix and each tribe's design-panel iterations through the harness could take days, and the owner wants to playtest soon.

Art is missing. A redesign of about 96 units plus 12 portraits already pending (content/portraits_pending.json) against Done means 5's 'unique art on every unit'. Keep unit identities where possible so the art carries over.
The target is written in stats (x1.5 a round, 2x the median) while fundamentals §2 says stat sums mislead. Without the S1 unit fixed, steps 2 and 4 can pass or fail on the wrong number.
A carry route in every tribe, plus the same four requirements for every tribe, may make tribes feel alike.
interrogate.smallest_path:
Fixed after: today, step 6 (build 8). Reordered, the owner's 'test the scale' question is answered at 2b. The full pool is fixed at step 6.

Steps, in order:
0. Harness: combat-start snapshots; 2 lines per tribe (tempo, and engine or fast tier) through the real shop and pool at rounds 6-16; field fights with sampled layouts; S1 in stats plus field win rate. Check on today's pool that it shows the flat shape.
1. A one-table reference from the audit's Battlegrounds data. Target v1 = September 2025, with numeric bars for growth, the 2x share, upsets, the round-8 leader's win rate and the progression jump. Rewrite Done means 2 and the reviewer rule now.
2. Levers, time-boxed: L1 and L6 (config) and L2 (an uncapped tribe bonus) first; L4 and L5 built once as engine keywords; an economy lever. S1 and upsets for each lever; the full suite on the finalist set.
2b. Strong-field mode, field ghosts and a lever build on today's pool. Three reward-lens reviewers play it. Checkpoint 1: does it feel like progress, and are snowballs uncommon?
3. Scale spec v2, budget v2 as bars plus a too-small test, then plan-interrogate.
4. Birds and Fairies redesigned, their lines rewritten by an independent author, passed on all bars. Checkpoint 2: reviewers play them. Then the other four tribes.
5. Bots buy answers on the scout and climb when they can afford it.
6. Build 8, playtest, the rest of the Done means.

Deferred:
- Hindsight search, until a tribe fails low.
- Bot rollouts, until a playtest shows the bot seats matter.
- Galaxy curves.
- The gold table, until something reads it.

Tell the owner after 2b and after each tribe pair whether the scale problem is fixed.

The orchestrator decides (ideation): the era (default September 2025), whether back-row answers are rare, carry route for most tribes or all.

fun.verdict: It will produce a well-measured game first and a fun one late. Harness-first is right, since the owner asked for sims, but the plan repeats the 6 Nov failure PLAN.md records: all six tribes (about 96 units) are redesigned before anyone plays, and the first feel check is step 6. The owner's 50/50 question was about feel ("does it feel like it has a nice flow?"); the plan answers it with curve sims. Fun is only a veto ("a fun critic doesn't flag it"): every pass bar is a metric, judges rank by harness numbers, and one template (engine, carry, one payback clock, a 30% answer bar) pushes six tribes toward one shape. Missing loops: economy greed, enablers and capstones, spells and heroes (still flat), golden highrolls, spike turns. Fix: a lean harness, then a two-variant scale build played before the redesign, then tribe pairs, each built and played.
cut: Step 0 part 3, hindsight search: nothing in the plan reads it. No pass bar, strong-field mode or ghost uses it. Defer until a bar needs an upper bound.

Step 1 as new work: the reference table already exists in evidence/fundamentals-audit/stat-scale-bg-galaxy.md (Sep 2025 and Nov 2026 by turn). Cite it. Defer the Galaxy VOD trial: there is no per-turn data, and it won't change target v1.
Step 0's damage model calibrated on lobby data: the scripted-line lobbies already give real Health for S3, so the plan builds Health twice.
More than two scripted lines per tribe on today's pool: pass 3 rewrites the tribes, so most of those lines get thrown away. A tempo line and an engine line per tribe are enough to test the levers.
Step 5 bot work (rollouts, adaptive climbing, saving, buying answers) before build 8: strong-field mode alone covers the playtest, and the owner says bots will 'never be elite' (9d).
Step 2's 'lands near target v1' as an exact done condition: a band is enough when play is meant to pick the era.
change: Insert a scale build after step 2: the adopted levers on today's pool, in two variants (the Sep 2025 shape and a steeper one). Reward-lens playtesters play both against strong-field opponents, and the build goes on the portal for the owner. Pick the era from play first, sims second. This answers the owner's 9c question by play.
Move a minimal strong-field mode ahead of that first playtest. It only needs the per-round fields the harness already builds.

Pass 3 ships a build and a short playtest after each tribe pair (Birds and Fairies first) before the next pair starts. This is PLAN.md's 6 Nov rule ('play a small slice first') and its rule of a build after each meaningful improvement.

Step 4 judges rank designs on reward moments, decisions created and tribe identity. Harness numbers act only as a guardrail band (same order of magnitude, no common snowball), as in 9c: 'balance comes second to fun'.

Each tribe's pass needs a positive fun bar, not just 'critic doesn't flag'. Name the turn its build comes online and the decision its engine creates, and get a playtester to point to a moment they felt stronger.

Turn S2's single payback clock and S4's 30% into reports with wide bands. Tribes should have different clocks and different ways to win. The owner's 2/2 that grows +1/+1 was an example, not a rule for every tribe.

Add an economy lever to step 2 (income growth, interest, or a gold engine that feeds stat buys). The owner's economy-to-tempo-to-greed loop (9d) has nothing to run on today, and S3 measures a greed line that no lever makes real (tally row 12: 'saving gold is a trap').

Add enablers, doublers and capstones to the step 4 brief (the owner's own enabler frame, 9a), plus one neutral of that kind as a step 2 lever. BG's highroll and discovery moments come from Brann- and Rivendare-style cards, not from the median curve.

Rescale heroes and spells alongside the levers. Bracken's +5/+5 cap, Mousewife's Mice sized by tier and the +1/+1 to +3/+3 spells vanish at 100/100, and heroes are the plan's stated source of 'every game plays differently'.

Split the upsets metric: count wins earned by scam, answers or placement apart from coin-flip targeting, and aim the variance budget at the first kind. The owner wants 'clever play' to beat a stat lead (9d).

Add a comeback target to the scripted-line lobbies. Treat playtest snowball reports as a signal for opponent and comeback design, not as noise until a sim reproduces them. It is the top tally complaint (14 reports), and compounding plus shorter games makes it worse.
Keep a lobby in strong-field mode: persistent rival seats with tribes and Health, so the owner has rivals and a 'who is running away' story, not a run of anonymous boards.
risks: The sims can match BG's curve shape while the game still feels samey. The shape is necessary but not enough; BG's fun lives in specific combo cards and spike turns that no metric here measures.

One template for every tribe (compounding engine, carry route, same payback clock, same answer bar) can produce six re-skins of BG's 'this game' Undead and Beast pattern. That fails Done means 3. L2's uncapped Supper for everyone points this way.
Agent playtesters and critics can't feel fun; the reward lens is a proxy. The owner is the only real fun test, and under this plan nothing new reaches him until step 6.

Common 'destroy or halve the biggest' answers feel bad for the player who loses a carry, and coin-flip upsets feel arbitrary. Without counterplay (shields, decoys, scouting), carry against answer becomes luck, not a duel.
Strong-field opponents drawn from strong and highroll lines could make most rounds a stomp, or make every opponent a frozen ghost. The owner would then judge the opponents, not the game.
Rounds 1-4 stay scripted (tally row 9) because the rework only touches round 8 onward. Every playtest opens on the dullest phase.
The lever loop can sprawl (more levers, combinations and critic panels) and push the first playable build back by days, when the owner wants to playtest soon.
Readability of 4-digit numbers is tested with one screenshot. Combat log and animation readability at that scale on phone are untested.
fun.smallest_path: Step 0, lean: combat-start snapshots, field fights, a tempo line and an engine line per tribe, and scripted-line lobbies, proved on today's flat curve. Step 2 on today's pool: L1-L6 plus an economy lever, one doubler-style neutral, and rescaled heroes and spells, at two scale variants (the Sep 2025 shape and a steeper one). Sims judge it within a band. Then a minimal strong-field mode with persistent rival seats, and build 8a, the scale build: reward-lens playtesters play both variants, and it goes on the portal for the owner. Pick the era from play first and sims second, and write budget v2 as a guardrail, not a price list. Pass 3 starts on Birds and Fairies, with designs ranked on reward moments and identity and harness numbers as a floor. Build and play that pair before starting the next. Bot rollouts, hindsight search and the Galaxy VODs wait until something reads them.

method.verdict: Not sound yet. The harness repeats the bot-lobby error in a new form. Scripted lines are bots, the field is built from them, and step 0's pass test checks them against the bot curve they replace. A strong-play harness should fail that test: the audit's own BG data puts top players at about 1.8x the mean board. Three parts measure the wrong thing. Solo goldfish runs skip fights, so they miss fight-earned Acorns, permanent combat gains, win-based gold and real damage, and a Health model fitted on bot lobbies patches the gap. The BG spread and upset targets come from perfect-game winners and their surviving opponents. And lever runs tune today's cards, which step 4 replaces. The cheapest trustworthy version: lines as Hard-brain profiles in the existing 8-seat bench lobbies, real fights, captured fight inputs re-fought in a round robin, damage variants replayed offline, and gates measured in outcomes. Approve after the changes.
cut: Hindsight search (step 0 part 3). Searching with knowledge of future shops gives neither an upper bound (the search is heuristic) nor a player. In a lobby it is ill-posed, because your buys change the pool other seats draw from. Scoring candidates by field fights costs about 10^5 fights per seed at about 5 ms each; scoring them by stats brings back the totals error. If needed, add it back in step 4 as a targeted combo-breaker for one tribe.

The calibrated Health model. It is fitted on bot lobbies under today's damage rule, so it is wrong for L6 by construction and for compounding boards, where a loss to a 2x board leaves more survivors. Real fights in lobbies give real damage, and damage-table variants can be replayed offline from the logged fight results.

Solo goldfish rollouts as the board generator. They have no fights, so they miss Acorns carried back from fights (combat.gd:301), won_last_combat/Rainy Day effects (effect_conditions.gd:73, recruit_extras.gd:23), Early Spoils and permanent combat carries: the whole of L3. With no other seats buying, nothing drains the pool, which inflates triple rates. Generate boards in all-line 8-seat lobbies instead.

L1–L5 as experiments on today's pool. L2, L4 and L5 are not data or config changes: src/core has no cleave, damage reduction, shield or venom, and 'target the biggest enemy' needs new targeting code. Step 4 also replaces the cards they act on. Keep L6, and replace the rest with one synthetic engine card (a growth-rate knob) and one synthetic proportional answer (a strength knob).
Step 2's Done line 'the curve with them adopted lands near target v1'. It tunes a pool that is about to be replaced. Done should mean the damage table, growth band and variance budget are chosen.

'Upsets: share of fights won by the side with fewer stats' as a gate. The BG figure (14–26%) counts fights that perfect-game winners won, in a snapshot that can't see deathrattles or shields. Adding hidden power raises it without making outcomes any less certain.
p99 as any gate. From 200–500 seeds per line it is the 2nd to 5th largest value, and the owner said rare highrolls don't matter (9d). Report it but don't gate on it.
change: Step 0 Done: replace 'reproduces today's flat curve within the lobby band' with known-answer tests. (a) A captured fight, re-fought, reproduces the in-game result exactly. (b) A line seat beats Hard in the existing head_to_head suite; if it doesn't, it isn't a strong line. (c) A planted broken card (a synthetic permanent +X/+X a turn, or uncapped Dozey) shows up as a tail and dominates, and a planted null card shows no change. Reuse the bench's plant_bad pattern.

Build scripted lines as profiles over the Hard brain (climb schedule, per-tribe card values, save threshold, committed tribe) and register them in BenchSuites.REGISTRY, rather than writing 12–18 new bots. Give each tribe's lines the same automated knob-tuning budget, and report the gain from tuning: a large gain means the lines aren't strong yet.

Capture each fight's full input for field fights: combat_board, combat_slots, fight_rules, tier and hero effects, through the path the ghost board already uses (game_session.gd _fight). benchmark_tournament.fight drops hero_effects, and STEP2's benchmark lost Rings, away Birds and counters, so a stats snapshot can't be re-fought.

Field fights use one fixed layout per board: the placer's, chosen blind against the field, in both orientations. Never use uniformly random layouts, because they understate carries, which are the thing under study. Use scout-adapted layouts only in S4. Report the line-by-line win matrix and the field's weights, not one field win rate.

Split metrics by purpose. Feel, in stats as the player sees them: own-board growth per turn, tier-up jumps against the player's own board, stats per gold. Snowballs and entropy, in outcomes: how often the round 8 leader wins, how often a board below the median at R8 finishes top 2, the share of R10–14 field pairs whose winner is 20–80% uncertain, and game length. Gate on outcomes, not on the share of boards at 2x the median in stats.

Field win rate is zero-sum within a round, so it can't show a ×1.5-a-round curve. If S1 needs a strength number that grows, use a ratio-scale one: the multiplier on the round's median field board that ties this board, found by about 16 bisection fights. Otherwise label S1 as stats.

Re-derive target v1 and state its limits. The September 2025 data is Firestone means only. The 13–23% at 2x the median and the 14–26% upset figures come from November 2026 replays of perfect-game winners and their opponents: survivors only, n=60 at turn 14, mixed skill and heroes. Use BG for the growth and feel curve; set the snowball targets in outcome terms.

Fix or drop the 'same seed' pairing in S2 and S3. shop_rng is one stream per seat (game_session.gd:577), and draw() picks against the current pool total (unit_pool.gd:103), so paired lines go out of sync after their first different action. Either derive shop draws per (seat, round, roll index), or treat comparisons as unpaired and size n for that.

Set sample sizes and CIs before any run. Fights cost about 5 ms each (72,000 in 364 s at R9) and Hard lobbies about 12.5 s each (spread: 333 in about 4,175 s). With one or two Godot processes, that is about 300–600 lobbies an hour, so 'under an hour' covers about one configuration plus a 64-board round robin per round, not thousands of boards each fought against a 100-board field.
Report spread within a line (shop luck) separately from spread between lines (strategy mix). The pooled 2x-median share rises from line mix alone, for example fast-tier against tempo at R8.

From build 8, log the owner's games in the snapshot format, so his boards can be placed on the lines' distribution. That is the only strong-player anchor available. Keep question 4 as an optional 10-minute calibration; don't block on it.
risks: Fixed scripts miss adaptive play: pivots, opportunistic highrolls, and many-action lines with no timer. The harness will then report a thinner tail than humans produce, designers will add compounding to reach the tail target, and the owner will snowball against the strong field. That is the same error the bots made, in the same direction.
Line quality leaks into tribe parity. A tribe with a worse-written line looks weak, and it also weakens the field that every other tribe is scored against.

BG's stat spread includes skill, hero and comp variety, plus hidden stats (deathrattles, shields). Matching it with Bramble's near-deterministic combat and shop luck alone will put too much luck into the game, and in outcome terms it will snowball far more than BG does.
Field fights from boards that can't be re-fought exactly (lost Rings, away Birds, Bellies, hero effects) score down the tribes with hidden state: Birds, Oozes and Bog.
Results from today's pool don't carry over. Engines, answers and keywords interact, so the redesigned pool will move the curve, and step 2 levers tuned on today's cards will mislead step 4.

Hitting the numeric target doesn't prove feel, and agents can't feel. If no owner session comes earlier, the first real check of 'do I feel stronger' arrives at build 8, after all six tribes have been redone.

Throughput: one or two Godot processes give about 300–600 lobbies an hour. Lever combinations × S1–S4 × lobbies can grow into days of runs, unless the configuration grid stays at a few synthetic knobs.
method.smallest_path: 1) Add combat-start snapshots and full fight-input capture (board, slots, rules, tier, hero effects) to bench.gd lobbies, with an exact re-fight test. 2) Write two lines per tribe (tempo; engine or carry) as Hard-brain profiles, plus one shared fast-tier/economy knob set, and tune the knobs with an equal budget per tribe. They pass when a line beats Hard head to head and a planted broken card shows up as a tail. 3) Run about 500–1,000 all-line 8-seat lobbies per configuration, with real fights, damage, pool depletion and heroes, and round robin a 64-board field per round from them. 4) Report feel metrics in stats and snowball/entropy metrics in outcomes. Replay damage and Health variants (L6) offline from the logged fights, with no new Godot runs. 5) Sweep one synthetic engine-growth knob and one synthetic proportional-answer knob to set the growth band and variance budget. 6) Go to step 4 and measure each redesigned tribe directly in the same lobbies. Get one playable tribe pair against the strong field to the owner before all six tribes are done. Defer hindsight search; drop the calibrated Health model and the today's-pool L1–L5 runs.

speed.verdict: The direction is right, and the "reproduce today's flat curve first" gate is the right honesty anchor. But the serial chain carries work that needs neither Godot nor the harness: the reference curves, the shared answers and keywords, and all six tribe designs on paper. Three two-tribe waves put design, build and measurement in series three times. They also measure new tribes against a field that is still mostly old flat tribes, so every early number has to be redone after the last wave. Some parts have no reader in any pass bar (hindsight search, the calibrated Health model, power-budget v2 before pass 3). Others redo work on cards about to be replaced (L2 and L3 on today's pool). Step 5 rebuilds the line lobbies that step 2 already makes. A faster honest order: start the harness, shared mechanics and six design panels together; run one lever sweep; build and measure all six tribes together; take opponents from the line policies; ship build 8 after one playtest round.
cut: Step 0 part 3, hindsight search: no pass bar in steps 2-4 reads it, and the owner is 'not worried about the top 1%' (9d). It is the most compute-heavy part. Defer it until a bar needs an upper bound, or use the owner's eye (fundamentals Q4) instead.
Step 0's Health model 'calibrated on the lobby data': the scripted-line lobbies in step 2 already give real Health with the real damage rule. Defer it.

Step 1's Galaxy VOD extension and any older-era study: target v1 is already set from data in hand (stat-scale-bg-galaxy.md has the Sep 2025 per-turn means and the replay spread). Consolidating it takes about an hour and can run beside step 0, not before step 2.

L2 as six hand-made engines on today's pool: that is pass 3 design work on cards that are being replaced. Use one synthetic, parameterised uncapped engine (a dial on growth rate) to find the rate, and let the designers build real engines to that setting.
L3 as an experiment: 'payoffs mostly permanent' is already decided (fundamentals section 3, step 4 requirements). Converting old combat-only cards to test it changes no decision.
Step 2's full matrix (S1-S4, upsets, line lobbies and a screenshot for every lever and combination): run S1 and upsets for each lever, and the full S2-S4 plus lobbies only on the chosen combination.

Step 3's power-budget v2 rewrite before pass 3: designers get no price table and the harness judges, so nothing in steps 4-6 reads it. Write v2 afterwards from measured cards. Keep only a one-page scale spec and the Done-means edit.
Step 3's second plan-interrogate: run it only if the spec changes this plan's steps.
'Every path choice in steps 2-4 goes to adversarial critics': gates stacked on gates. Keep one critic panel at the lever pick and the judges in step 4.
Step 5's rollout valuation and the bot rework: the owner says bots won't be elite (9d). Line-policy seats plus strong-field mode give strong opponents for much less work.

Step 6 holding build 8 'until all three judge it very good': deliver after round 6's agreed fixes, and keep iterating while the owner plays (PLAN.md: a build goes out after each meaningful improvement).
change: Start four tracks on day one: Sol branch 1 builds the trimmed harness; Sol branch 2 builds the shared mechanics; workflow agents run reference-curves.md and all six tribe design panels. Paper designs need no code branch, so the two-branch rule doesn't stop them.

Replace 'two tribes at a time' with all six designed in parallel, and built on one content branch with one commit and one scope review per tribe. Then measure all six together against a field made of the new pool. That removes two serial waves and the mixed old/new field. Hedgerow gets a light pass (caps off, Lollop tribe-only, permanent payoffs), since the owner sees 'nothing fundamentally too wrong' with it.
Brief the designers with the target shape and frame that are already decided. Each design names its engine's rate as a parameter, so the lever sweep picks a setting instead of forcing a redesign.

Make the scripted strong lines data-driven: a per-tribe card priority list plus climb, save and engine settings, on top of the existing Hard evaluation. Each tribe's designers write the list as part of the design, so the lines survive the redesign instead of being re-scripted.
Move L4 and L5 (answers that target the biggest enemy, damage reduction, shield, cleave) into the shared-mechanics branch now. They are lever tests and final neutral content in one build.
Put a phone-size render of 4-digit stats on day one, in branch 2. If big numbers don't read, the target era drops before any design is built on it.

Fold step 5 into the harness's second slot during the tribe build. Bot seats run the line policies, strong-field mode draws from the field snapshots, bots buy an answer when the scout shows a carry, and ghosts become field boards.

Plan the Godot throughput. The flock wrapper runs one Godot process at a time; full bot games ran about 10 fights a second in the soaks. Run the lever and tribe sweeps on cloud VMs (owner-agreed for heavy runs, 8 Nov), and size seeds and field to fit, or the sims become the slowest part.
Start portraits for the new units as soon as the designs settle on names. The plan never mentions art, and Done means 5 needs unique art on every unit; 12 pass 2 units already lack it.

Measure curve shape (growth per round, p90/p50, the share of boards at twice the median) in combat-start stats, so it compares like for like with the Battlegrounds reference. Use field win rate for tribe parity, S2 and S4.
Optional: after the lever pick, export a 'scale preview' of today's pool with the adopted levers, against line-policy seats, so the owner can feel the new scale while pass 3 builds.
risks: Designs start before the lever sweep. If the sweep shows the target needs a different variance or damage model, some paper designs need rework. The decided frame and the engine-rate parameter limit this, and paper design is cheap.
One content branch with six tribes is a large review surface, and one bad tribe could block the merge. Keep per-tribe commits with per-tribe scope reviews, so a failing tribe can be held back.
Local Godot runs are serialized. Without cloud VMs, the parallel plan's critical path is still sim time, and the speed-up shrinks to the design work.

Line policies written by agents play below a strong human, so measured curves come out flatter than real play. With the hindsight search deferred, the only upper-bound check is the owner's eye on about eight boards.
Field win rate is relative to the field. Compared directly with Battlegrounds' stat curves, the shape test is circular. Measure the shape in stats.
